body:
Three positions are on the table. The account proposed a mechanism — agreements drift because nobody records them — and a remedy: a shared note, a weekly check-in, and one careful approach to the avoiding friend. The objection demoted the mechanism, split memorial from normative disagreement, and reversed the remedy's ranking. The rival added two more readings and a probe. Here is what I would use, revise, and drop, and on what grounds.

I am dropping the account's diagnostic confidence and its original test. The grounds are the objection's: 'watch whether what-was-agreed disputes fall' is readable as support whichever way it comes out — a fall could be memory disputes resolving while the substantive disagreement persists; no fall could mean the disputes were never memorial. A test that cannot fail is not a test. The rival's point also stands: nothing in the stated material forces the memory-gap reading over scope-ambiguity-at-the-moment-of-agreement or over the standing-negotiation reading, and the slide from 'no shared record' to 'make a shared record' treats a plausible diagnosis as an established one. The retrospective half (agreements drifted unrecorded) is supportable; the prospective half (recording will stop the drift) is not yet earned. I am also demoting the weekly check-in from first position, on grounds the account itself supplied: it assumes all three can talk together, which is exactly what the avoidance puts in question. Prescribing more group meeting to the person who left group meetings is the proposal's weak edge.

I am keeping the rival's probe as the first move, revised in two ways. First, the objection's warning applies to it: the probe returns what each person now reports, not what was agreed, and the reports are part of what is in dispute. It is a lens on divergence, not a route to the truth of the past. Second, I would pair it with a classification — do the disagreements sound like scope (what the task covers), recurrence (how often, until when), timing (by what point), or none of these? That baseline is what makes any later test discriminating: after an intervention, re-classify. If scope and timing disputes fall while fairness-flavored disputes persist, that says something a bare count of arguments never could.

The probe also quietly resolves the standoff between the objection and the rival over the avoiding friend. Conducted one-to-one with each flatmate, it is the objection's priority — attend to the person, not the artifact — wearing the rival's safer framing: ask what they thought had been agreed, not why they avoid the conversations. If the friend will not talk even at that, that is data, and it strengthens the avoidance-central reading. I would add one honesty the rival stopped short of: no framing removes the risk of being heard as the subject of a conversation about one's own withdrawal. The available mitigation is naming the risk aloud — if this conversation is also a bad one, say so and I will stop — and treating a refusal as an answer rather than an obstacle.

On the record: I accept the objection's distinction. A note settles who said what; it does not settle what 'done' or 'this week' means when schedules keep moving. So the record and the rival's scope statement fuse into one practice or neither is worth doing: state scope at the moment of agreement ('bins, tonight's run, not bin duty'), and the note is simply where those statements live. A bare note relocates the argument onto the note — who wrote it, who is on it — which under the standing-negotiation reading is a new venue, not a fix.

One thing the stated material licenses that none of the three inputs used: the schedules change. Person-relative assignments ('A does dishes') break against that fact by design; trigger-relative ones ('dishes when the sink is full', 'bin night goes to whoever is home') absorb it. This is a proposal, and it carries a named failure mode: trigger rules load work onto whoever is home most or has the lowest mess threshold, which can quietly rebuild unfairness while looking neutral. If it is tried, the load distribution needs its own occasional look.

Finally, a generalization the three inputs earned separately: each flagged that a favored artifact gets read socially — the note as surveillance, the check-in as more of the failed thing, the record as the argument's new venue. That is one observation in three costumes. If the disputes are partly about standing, nothing the asker introduces is neutral; it arrives as the asker's move. The mitigation is not a better artifact but an announced purpose and a disclaimed authority: 'I am not appointing myself chore manager; if this feels like a takeover, say so and we drop it.'

Still open, and I am not closing them: whether the standing reading is true, whether load is unequal, whether the avoidance predates the schedule changes, whether this household wants any process at all. Nothing in the material ranks a mediator, a redivision of chores, or formalization. Probe, classify, then adopt the narrowest practice the classification supports — that is the sequence the material permits, not the one it commands.
commitments:
Taking this up involves several separable commitments.

The central one is a demotion: I am committing to treat the memory-gap mechanism as one live reading among three rather than the central one. That claim has a stated failure condition. If the probe elicits reports that sound like someone losing track of a shared understanding rather than people having held divergent understandings all along, my demotion loses its support and the account's original diagnosis is partially rehabilitated — I would want that to count against this continuation rather than be explained away.

The sequence — probe, classify, then adopt the narrowest practice — is a proposal with named costs. Three separate conversations can be read as interrogation, and one of them is with a person already withdrawing. If the probe itself pushes the avoiding friend further away, that counts against my sequencing, and the right response may be to stop building process rather than to reframe the probe and try again.

My sharpened test inherits a weakness the rival already flagged: it classifies reported positions, and the reports are part of what is disputed. If self-reports in this household prove too noisy or too self-serving to classify, the sharpened test collapses back into the account's uninformative one, and the objection's stricter point — that no cheap test separates the readings — would stand. The check-in demotion is likewise conditional: if the friend's avoidance turns out to be specific to chore talk rather than to group conversation generally, that demotion loses its grounds and the check-in becomes defensible again. I would want that revision made openly if it comes.

The trigger-relative task definitions are my own addition, and I flag the failure mode in advance: load concentrating on whoever is home most or has the lowest mess threshold. If that occurs, it is a failure of the proposal and should revise or kill it, not a fact about the household's character. The unilateral fallback — the asker stating their own scope each time they agree to something — is also mine, and it can be read as passive-aggressive point-scoring; if it is read that way even with the risk named, I would drop it rather than escalate.

The social-reading generalization is a lens built from three single flags in the inputs, not a finding about this flat. If some artifact there is experienced as genuinely neutral, the lens is too strong and should be narrowed rather than defended.

What I am not committing to: any ranking of mediator, chore redivision, or formalization; any claim about which reading is true; any claim about load distribution, the avoidance's history, or whether the asker contributes to the pattern. Those remain open questions the material does not decide. The sequence I propose is what the visible facts permit, not what they command.
